proposals.evidence_note: Own1996 answer explicitly relates the framework to Mothers of Invention and her ending. The resource and her criticism coexist;no claim of personal supervision or adoption of all Woodward interpretations. His original essays and complete1996 book remain unread.

proposals.relationship: Faust argues that Woodward’s burden-of-Southern-history account changes when examined through African Americans’ and white Southern women’s experiences.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1996 interview says Woodward focuses on white Southern men and identifies her ending as taking issue with that emphasis. This is a particular representational qualification,not dismissal of Woodward’s entire career or claim that the two other groups share one historical burden.

proposals.evidence_note: Own2014 first-person account credits a plural cohort;own2023 retrospect recalls Genovese’s insights at meetings and explicitly assesses his account of ideology. Elizabeth Fox-Genovese retains intellectual and coauthor credit,especially for the later trilogy. This is a bounded scholarly resource,not sole mentoring or adherence to paternalism. Original books remain unread;2023 selected substantial indexed primary passages checked despite direct-page failures.

proposals.relationship: Faust rejects Genovese’s paternalism framework while arguing that its disappearance leaves unresolved questions about slaveholders’ self-justifying ideas.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2023 address calls paternalism flawed and distances herself from rehabilitation of Genovese. She retains his acknowledgment of cruelty,his later revisions,and the problem of ideology that remains after rejection. Elizabeth Fox-Genovese is coauthor of the later master-class studies;criticism does not assign those books to Eugene alone or equate understanding enslavers with endorsement. Complete original books unread.
primary_locators: SIHC2023,paragraph beginning The concept of paternalism is now dead and gone;closing paragraphs beginning But that means we need to study those ideas;earlier trilogy/Fatal Self-Deception discussion and notesvii/xi.

proposals.relationship: Faust uses Johnson’s challenge to paternalism to explain how the slave market unsettled accounts of reciprocal master–slave obligations.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2023 historiographical reconstruction identifies Soul By Soul and the subsequent criticism as a resource for this reassessment,alongside Michael Tadman and others. It is not agreement with every claim of the later New History of Capitalism;her separate criticism of that approach remains. Johnson’s original book/articles and Tadman’s original research were not read.
primary_locators: SIHC2023,paragraph beginning The attacks on paternalism that Walter Johnson had begun to elaborate in Soul By Soul;preceding slave-trade discussion;notesix–x.

proposals.relationship: Faust questions whether the New History of Slavery’s Capitalism,including Johnson’s work,adequately explains slaveholders’ ideas and regional cultural differences.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2023 address names Johnson’s River of Dark Dreams,Beckert’s Empire of Cotton and Edward Baptist’s The Half Has Never Been Told as three major statements before criticizing the shared framework’s concentration on material self-interest. Baptist and Jones-Rogers are separate,more individually detailed examples;their specific claims are not reassigned to this target. Faust concedes possible economic connections while asking whether worldviews remained distinct. Original monographs and other economic critics’ articles unread.

proposals.relationship: McPherson questions Faust’s weighting of the Civil War’s human cost against its transformative achievements in emancipation,citizenship and equality.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2008 review of Faust and Mark Schantz distinguishes their arguments and addresses both at its end. McPherson credits Faust’s national-cemetery argument but ranks the Reconstruction Amendments as still more nationalizing;he grants their chosen topic and praises their sensitive,eloquent research. This is qualified criticism,not rejection of studying death or a claim that Faust omitted emancipation entirely. Original books unread.
